messages:
lee: Heads-up — saw a sudden tail-latency bump on a production host around 01:20 UTC. P50 fine, p99 jumped from ~120ms to ~480ms for short seqs (<=64). :eyes:
maya: Ugh. Any obvious request pattern changes?
lee: Early profiler snap shows frequent kernel re-selection while handling concurrent small requests + one long streaming session. Looks like thrash between fast-opt kernel and a fallback that disables fused attention.
rob: Can you paste the profiler logs?
lee: Sure — paste below (trimmed):
```
2026-03-12T01:20:12Z host=iw-03 profiler: kernel_select: model=red-v2 seq=32 concurrency=24 selected=fast_attention
2026-03-12T01:20:12Z host=iw-03 profiler: kernel_select: model=red-v2 seq=1024 concurrency=3 selected=fallback_autovec
2026-03-12T01:20:13Z host=iw-03 profiler: kernel_select: model=red-v2 seq=32 concurrency=26 selected=fallback_autovec
2026-03-12T01:20:13Z host=iw-03 profiler: kernel_select: model=red-v2 seq=16 concurrency=28 selected=fast_attention
```
lee: Note the same host handling a few 1k-seq tool calls while the rest are small — selection flips every few ms.
alex: That matches noisy-tenant behavior — one tenant with tool-calls using long chains. Did KV cache hit rates change?
lee: KV hit rate dropped from 93% -> 58% during window. Likely cache eviction from the long seqs.
maya: Streaming backpressure could be making the runtime queue long and increasing concurrency for small requests, forcing different kernel heuristics.
rob: Any traces for the streaming session?
lee: Got a trace id: trace-20260312-01-20-ixw. Key parts: streaming session holds a persistent slot, long generation (3k tokens), intermittent function/tool calls that trigger synchronous CPU ops.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Rolling restart of inference-worker/iw-03 scheduled to reclaim memory, ETA 5m.
alex: Before restart, can we do a targeted mitigation — pin kernel policy for short seqs to avoid thrash? Maybe force using small-seq kernel when seq<=64 regardless of global concurrency heuristics.
maya: We'd need quick config change. Risk: might lose perf for medium sequences if wrong kernel chosen.
rob: But current tail is hurting everyone. I'm +1 for a short-lived override. Who can push?
sre_oncall: I'll approve emergency config if you sign off on rollback plan.
lee: I'll prepare a hotfix: change kernel_policy: prefer_fast_for_small=true and reduce eviction aggressiveness for kvcache for 2m. Rolling change to five hosts first.
alex: Also add a quick guard in scheduler to deprioritize threads from streaming sessions if they're saturating CPU/io.
maya: Can we also collect a full p99/p50 diff and KV eviction events for the next 10m to validate?
lee: Yes — enabling detailed eviction logs and kernel decision trace for 10m.
rob: After change, monitor for degradation in medium/large workloads. If we see >5% slowdown, roll back.
lee: Pushing config to canary hosts now.
lee: Update — 2/5 hosts show p99 back down to ~130ms within 90s. KV hit rate rising.
sre_oncall: Great. Keep a close eye for regressions, and capture heap / GPU memory stats.
maya: Logged follow-up ticket with root-cause hypothesis: 'long streaming tool-calls cause KV churn -> kernel-selection thrash -> tail latency spike'. Assigning to eng-runtime/lee+rob.
rob: Blameless postmortem later. For long term: think about kernel-selection hysteresis + tenant isolation for streaming-heavy flows.
lee: Agree. I'll start a small RFC for kernel hysteresis and scheduler QoS for streaming sessions.
lee: Thanks all :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Restart completed on iw-03.
lee: Closing thread — will drop notes in the incident doc and link the traces.
